mytest_moreit_seekable.problem_statement: In more_itertools, seekable(iterable, maxlen=0) is meant to provide peek()/truthiness lookahead without retaining consumed items — but each peek() call consumes the next item from the source and, because a maxlen=0 deque cannot store it, wraps the source in a fresh itertools.chain to put it back. Calling peek() or bool() repeatedly therefore accumulates one chain object per call: memory grows linearly (a tracemalloc check over 10000 peek/bool iterations retains far more than 256 KB) and each call gets slower. Make zero-cache lookahead storage bounded — for example by keeping the lookahead in the source iterator (a peekable) instead of the result cache — so repeated peek()/bool() calls retain no per-call objects, peek() keeps returning the correct next item (and raising StopIteration or returning the default at exhaustion), and iteration order, seek()/elements() behavior, and all other seekable behavior stay unchanged.

mytest_packaging_tokend.problem_statement: packaging's tokenizer treats a bare end-of-input marker with the regular-expression construct that also matches immediately before a final newline. As a result, a Marker or Requirement string that ends with a line break silently parses: `Marker('python_version >= "3"\n')` and `Requirement('name>=1\n')` are accepted even though embedded or trailing line breaks should make the input invalid. A trailing line break must raise InvalidMarker / InvalidRequirement, while a string ending in ordinary horizontal whitespace (spaces or tabs) must continue to parse successfully.
